problem.title: Finding information is not enough. Applicable evidence is required.
problem.intro: BMMS — Maritime Regulatory Applicability & Evidence Intelligence is an evidence-first and provenance-first engineering decision-support system. It preserves the distinctions between source version, authority, applicability, evidence sufficiency and authorised human decision. It is not a chatbot, PMS or ERP.

issues.title: Sources live in different places and formats
issues.text: Regulatory texts, class publications, manufacturer documents and operational records are kept in separate systems. Information on the same topic never appears in one place.

issues.title: Choosing the right version is a task of its own
issues.text: Rules and documents are revised over time. An event must be assessed against the version in force at that date; the latest version is not always the right one.

issues.title: The conclusion survives, its basis is lost
issues.text: When an assessment is written into a report, the exact section of the exact document it relied on is often not recorded. Verifying or challenging it later becomes difficult.

issues.title: Relevant is not the same as applicable
issues.text: A paragraph found by search may be relevant to the topic. Whether it applies to that ship, that equipment and that condition must be shown separately.

figure.title: FIG. 2 · SOURCE FRAGMENTS
figure.foot: Once every fragment is recorded in the same way, with its source, version and location within the document, it becomes comparable and traceable. Source families are admitted only to the extent that processing rights have been established.

approach.title: From source to decision, an unbroken chain.
approach.intro: The core idea of BMMS is that every step stays attached to the one before it. If a link in the chain cannot be established, the system does not fill the gap with a guess; it shows the missing link.

legend.text: Implemented on the server side and exercised by automated tests. Does not mean an end-user product interface.
Core data model and services exist; scope is being extended.

approach.canonLabel: THE FULL CHAIN IN THE PROJECT DOCUMENTS

steps.title: Source and version
steps.text: A document is recorded with its issuing authority, version and, where known, effective date. The raw document is stored unchanged; a correction is added as a new version.

steps.title: Passage
steps.text: The document is split into sections with stable identities. A citation points to a specific passage in a specific version, so the same citation still shows the same text years later.

steps.title: Applicability
steps.text: Whether a retrieved passage applies to this ship, this equipment and this event is assessed separately. If the context is insufficient, the state remains “indeterminate”.
steps.note: The authority, revision and applicability foundation is in place; its scope is being extended.

steps.title: Obligation and evidence
steps.text: Applicable requirements are linked to the evidence claimed to satisfy them. Missing evidence does not mean the requirement does not exist.
steps.note: Links between claims and evidence exist in the backend. Establishing a complete obligation set is a separate line of development.

steps.title: Expert decision
steps.text: The final assessment belongs to an authorised person. The reviewer and the person holding decision authority are kept distinct; AI output is not treated as verified evidence.
steps.note: Review status is held in the data model; the reviewer interface is at prototype stage.

steps.title: Assurance state
steps.text: The conclusion is recorded together with its scope, the source versions used, the evidence set, the decision authority and any residual obligations. It is re-evaluated when conditions change.

end.text: Records are written to an append-only audit history. An old record is never deleted; it is superseded by a new one.

ready.label: READY FOR EXPERT DECISION
ready.text: The context makes {passage} applicable; the evidence has been linked to that passage. Whether the evidence is sufficient is decided by an authorised expert.

missing.label: EVIDENCE MISSING
missing.text: An applicable requirement was identified ({passage}), but there is no evidence showing it is met. Missing evidence does not mean the requirement does not exist.

unknown.label: INDETERMINATE · NO CONCLUSION
unknown.text: Without the ship's position, it cannot be determined which limit applies. The system does not guess; it records the missing context and holds the assessment open.

demo.note: Representative scenario. The topic is simplified from the fuel sulphur limits under MARPOL Annex VI. Passage and document names are illustrative; they are neither quotations from a real source nor output produced by BMMS. The purpose is to show the states the system is designed to distinguish.

principles.title: What does trustworthiness rest on?
principles.intro: In BMMS, quality is not measured only by the rate of correct answers. The basis, scope and uncertainty of a conclusion must also be explicit, measurable and auditable.
principles.invariantAria: Retrieved, authoritative, current, applicable and sufficient are not equivalent.
principles.invariantCaption: The core distinction in the project's rule set: retrieving a passage does not mean it comes from an authoritative source, is current, applies to this case, or is sufficient on its own. These distinctions are defined as invariants in the code and project documents.

items.title: Every claim is tied to a source
items.text: A source record carries the issuing authority, title, version, effective date where known, and content identity. Citations are passage-level and pinned to a specific version.

items.title: What enters the system is explicit
items.text: The rights basis on which each source family was admitted is recorded. Being able to access a document does not mean having the right to process it; material with unclear rights is held for review.

items.title: The unknown stays unknown
items.text: When the basis cannot be established, an “indeterminate” or “review required” state is recorded explicitly. Having identified no gap does not prove that the case is closed.

items.title: Decisions belong to an authorised person
items.text: Model output is never stored as verified evidence without an explicit, recorded human approval. Having reviewed a record is not the same as holding decision authority.

items.title: Which method ran is never hidden
items.text: The default retrieval method is lexical. Semantic and hybrid methods were tested in an experiment with pre-registered criteria; because they did not meet the promotion criterion, they remain experimental and are never switched on silently.

items.title: An easy test is a failed test
items.text: Alongside the aggregate score, critical failures such as false closure, missed obligations and failure to abstain are tracked separately. A calibration set on which current models hit a ceiling was marked “too easy” and not used for ranking.

discipline: Automated quality gates on every change

stages.title: Pre-Pilot R&D & Validation
stages.intro: BMMS is currently in research, validation and controlled pilot preparation.

columns.title: Core foundation
items: Immutable evidence store with content identity
Passage extraction from documents, stable passage identity
Lexical evidence retrieval and evidence bundles
Regulatory authority, revision and applicability foundation
Semantic and hybrid retrieval experiment (pre-registered; not made default)

columns.title: Controlled pilot preparation
items: Testing the workflow under real conditions in a controlled, single-organisation setting, with sources whose rights basis is established
columns.note: Pilot readiness is not considered complete until it is demonstrated with runtime evidence on a specific release.

columns.title: Accepted development direction
items: Multiple source families: IMO / SOLAS / ISM, MARPOL / MEPC, IACS, OCIMF and authorised manufacturer documents (where rights permit)
Operational modules for equipment, maintenance, certificate and obligation tracking
Signed export and verifiable evidence package
columns.note: An accepted architecture direction is not an authorisation to implement.

stages.honesty: BMMS is not presented as a broad production deployment, an accredited product, a commercial success or a completed customer pilot.

research.intro: The BMMS research programme treats every link from source material to authorised human decision as a distinct validation problem.
